thread:
Alex K.: quick heads-up — saw a pattern in the profiler: when batches form with large token budgets and many cached KV slices, GPU memory spikes and we hit soft OOMs on the T4 pool. reproducer attached in gist. can we triage?
Mae L.: ugh, saw a few alerts this morning too. which config was this? continuous batching default?
Alex K.: yes, continuous batching w/ token_budget=2048, kv_cache_enabled=true. spike happens during batch formation, before kernel dispatch.
Chris P.: do we have a histogram of kv cache footprint per request? need p50/p95 of cached bytes.
Jin W.: grabbing that now. initial quick look: p95 cached token bytes ~ 600MB/request on those models. combined into batch 6-8x -> >4GB. on T4 with reserved model memory that pushes us over.
Sarah M.: that sounds like classic aggregation problem. options: 1) reduce per-batch token_budget, 2) preflight sample to estimate kv footprint before admitting, 3) kernel fallback that supports streaming KV evictions, 4) conservative headroom floor based on measured cache.
Alex K.: thinking about a lightweight "memory anchoring" heuristic: estimate expected KV bytes for the batch by summing p50 footprints for the incoming queue and clamp token_budget so estimated KV + model footprint < threshold.
Mae L.: love the name :laughing: Could implement as admission check inside batcher. cheap sampling: sample first 3 items in queue, multiply by batch size? avoid full scan.
Chris P.: careful with bias — short requests could under-estimate. maybe use an EWMA per route for kv footprint and a short preflight sample to nudge it.
Jin W.: EWMA per route + sample sounds good. also add a kernel-route flag: if estimated KV high, route to kernel variant with lower memory cozying (quantized-run or chunked-attn).
Alex K.: pseudo-config: 
```
batcher {
  mode: continuous
  token_budget: 2048
  kv_memory_budget_ratio: 0.75
  sample_count: 3
  ewma_alpha: 0.2
}
```
Admission: if estimated_kv + model_resident_mem > kv_memory_budget_ratio * gpu_available_mem -> reduce token_budget = max(min_budget, scaled_budget)

Mae L.: what about latency regressions? reducing token_budget increases number of batches -> higher per-request latency and cost. need to track unit-cost impact.
Sarah M.: agree. we can add an observability metric: "batch_adjustment_reason" tag (kv_anchor|latency|kernel_fallback) and track tokens/latency/unit_cost pre/post.
Chris P.: deployment plan: small canary on a subset of T4 nodes with metric alarms. if unit_cost delta > 5% for 10m -> revert or tighten anchor.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: runtime/v3.14.2 -> cluster=t4-canary (10 nodes). tracking group=eng-runtime.
Jin W.: I'll wire the ewma + sample code this afternoon and add feature flag `kv_memory_anchor_v2` behind runtime flags.
Alex K.: can you also add a debug trace in batch logs that prints estimated_kv, model_resident_mem, chosen_token_budget for failed admissions? just once per minute to keep volume low.
Jin W.: yep. adding log lines like: `BATCH_ADMIT trace est_kv=XXMB model_mem=YYMB budget=ZZ` and a metric counter `batch_admit_kv_anchor{route,action}`.
Mae L.: I'll create the perf dashboard panels: batch_admits, avg_chosen_token_budget, unit_cost_by_route, batch_adjustment_reason. link to alert thresholds in ops doc.
Chris P.: also open a short-lived experiment to try kernel fallback as a second throttle: if anchor reduces quality too much, prefer routing to low-memory kernel and keep token budget. compare both approaches.
Sarah M.: good. action items: Jin implement EWMA+sample + logs; Mae dashboard + alerts; Chris setup kernel-fallback experiment; Alex to prioritize dataset of failing traces and add to repro; I'll coordinate canary monitoring.
Alex K.: thanks team. ping me in thread with pr links.
Mae L.: noted. assigning follow-ups in linear. :thumbsup: 
Chris P.: will add a tiny script to replay real queue shapes against the new admission logic — want to simulate cost/latency.
Jin W.: PR will reference ticket INF-4123. aiming for canary today.
Sarah M.: if anything spikes, we can revert the feature flag immediately.
Alex K.: perfect. thanks all.
